reviews.text: Comparable to the best tofu houses in South Korea, BCD is well known even amongst Korean celebrities as a must visit when in LA. Visited here 5 times in my first week in LA. Have been many more times since, including introducing my Korean gf to the place. She also admitted to BCD being better than most Korean tofu houses and agreeing that it compares to the best places in Seoul. A must visit. Special mention to the Galbi set and the marinated raw crab set. I myself get the tripe and intestine tofu with danger level spicy, but the kimchi tofu is also quite good. My gf went with the seafood tofu which was also tasty. Go here. The one on Wilshire is better than the others.

BCD Tofu House in LA delivered a reliably satisfying experience, especially if you’re in the mood for comforting Korean food served quickly and generously. The signature soon tofu came out boiling hot with a rich, well-seasoned broth that paired nicely with the soft curds of tofu and your choice of protein. One of the highlights is the complimentary dishes that arrive alongside the stew — from crispy fried fish to fresh kimchi — adding variety and a homestyle feel to the meal. Portions are hearty, rice is perfectly cooked and served in a stone pot for that delicious crust, and service moves at a brisk pace even during busy hours. It’s not a place known for culinary surprises, but if you’re craving classic sundubu done right in the heart of LA’s Korean comfort-food scene, BCD remains a dependable go-to.

It's easy to see why it's so popular. We had about a 45-minute wait for dinner, but the waiting patio had outdoor heaters, which made it quite bearable. The restaurant has a lively, bustling atmosphere that feels authentic and inviting, perfect for a casual meal with friends or family.

We ordered a few of their classic soondubu (soft tofu) stews, and each one was piping hot, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned. The tofu itself was silky and fresh, and the broths had that rich, comforting depth that makes you want to keep sipping. The banchan (side dishes) were plentiful, fresh, and varied, which always adds to the experience. The food was soo good that we went back the following day for lunch and tried their spicy raw crab (양념게장)—absolutely fresh and delicious, bursting with flavor. LA Galbi and seafood pancake were very good too.

Service was friendly and attentive despite the busy environment, and our food came out quickly once we were seated. Plenty of parking spaces, which makes it convenient even during busy hours :)

I came because I wanted Korean food because I only ate Western food every day in LA, but I think it doesn't taste good either.

The taste can't keep up with the price.
That's too bad.

I think it's mandatory to visit because I'm just a Korean.

It's a kind of marketing power by popularity.

Tried the seafood tofu soon soup and it tasted really good — rich, comforting, and full of flavor. The portion size was just right. Overall a very satisfying meal. Would definitely come back if I’m craving Korean food.

I love the couple of AYCE KBBQ spots up here near my home base, but K-Town (Ktow adjacent?) KBBQ is a whole different beast. This place was sooo good. Three of us came a little bit after open on a sunday and we got straight into it. Beef belly, beef bulgogi, and brisket mostly, some pork belly too. The rice, kimchi, and Ssamjang was flowing as the meat came off the stone, and in a matter of an hour we where all totally stuffed.

The atmosphere is great and by the time we left it was already getting fuller, slightly smoky, and so perfect with all the smells and clattering dishes.

I wish they had had more flavors of Maekgolli but I was delighted to finally try it, sooo good with the fatty meats and spicy sour flavors of the side dishes.

The staff is way more active than other KBBQ places up here, adding meat, flipping, turning, adjusting the stove, and if this is the default for Ktown KBBQ then a I love it and wished it was done like this everywhere.. it felt like they where trying to give us more and more as gracious hosts versus the more passive approach at other KBBQ places I've been to outside LA. Ask for more of any side dish or sauce and it's there in seconds, not minutes, incredible staff. The quality and taste of everything just like the service was exceptional, and you pay accordingly for it... It's not cheap. But I could easily come here solo and essentially eat one incredible giant meal for the day with drinks for like 50 bucks and feel sooo good until the next day. Go here, it's so bomb.

Food:
The food itself was very basic and nothing extraordinary, especially for an AYCE Korean BBQ spot in Koreatown where competition is high. The only notable difference compared to most AYCE places is that they cook the meat for you, which some may appreciate. Flavor-wise though, nothing stood out or justified the hype or the wait.

Service:
This is the primary reason for the one-star review. Service from Sally and Sarah was extremely poor. Sally in particular seemed very unhappy to be there—she was nonverbal, avoided eye contact, and provided little to no communication. When we asked for simple things like more rice, she would nod but then never return with it. It felt dismissive and frustrating. Sarah eventually came around toward the end of the meal and provided better service, but the overall experience had already been soured. Poor service can ruin a meal, and unfortunately that’s exactly what happened here.

Ambiance:
The restaurant was very crowded with a long wait time. Parking is also a major issue in the area, adding to the inconvenience.

A solid and authentic Korean BBQ spot. The pork dishes turned out to be our family’s favorite. I’d recommend visiting on a weekday, as Friday evenings get very busy. When we went on a Friday night, the service felt a bit rushed since our waitress was handling multiple tables at once. Also, we left smelling strongly of BBQ afterward, so the ventilation could definitely be improved.

Okay so I guess I found my new favorite AYCE KBBQ spot and I'm mad cause I can't be there everyday to enjoy what was the best KBBQ I've ever had, but I will be back... often! What can I say, the proteins were top notch, and the side dishes may have been the star of the show, not to mention the best bulgogi meat I've ever had. We came in around 10:00pm on a busy Saturday night and we were a party of 7 so a 35 minute wait really wasn't bad. The place is on the smaller end of any other KBBQ spots I've been to, so it's a bit more cramped for bigger parties. They have this stone grill and clean it with shredded radishes which is unlike another spot I've been to. Do your self a favor, pay extra compared to other spots, but experience this culinary delicacy. Please note you may be lucky to find street parking or else its valet since it's in a small strip mall.

Slightly expensive for a KBBQ but the meat quality and service (refilling of sides and water; cutting up our meat) was fantastic. They sat 11 of us, though they don’t guarantee such large tables even if you call before hand.
